summary: MCP toolkit that gives coding agents IDE-like abilities: find symbols, navigate code and make precise edits.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Serena gives coding agents IDE-like tools for semantic code retrieval, editing, refactoring and debugging. It works at the symbol level using language servers (or a JetBrains backend) and connects to any client or LLM through MCP.
sixtySeconds.problem: Agents that read and edit code as plain text waste tokens and make clumsy changes. Serena lets them find and edit exactly the right symbols.
whoFor: Users of Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for agent-first, symbol-level tools across many languages that plug into any MCP client.

overview: Install with uv tool install -p 3.13 serena-agent; the serena command then becomes available. Don't install it from MCP or plugin marketplaces, which the README says have outdated commands.
Run serena init to set up the language server backend (or add -b JetBrains for the JetBrains plugin). Some languages need extra dependencies; see the language support page.

Connect it to your client with a launch command or by running the MCP server in HTTP mode; the docs cover Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop and IDEs. Licensing: the Serena app is GPL-3.0-or-later, and the SolidLSP part is MIT.
